requirement_text.REQ-364:
Implements REQ-363's design artefact exactly — no new schema decisions here, this requirement is implementation of an already-validated design, matching this project's own CODE-DESIGNER-then-ELIXIR-DEV split for every other schema-bearing feature.

SCOPE: the `Letflow.Help` context module (naming follows this project's existing per-domain-context convention, e.g. `Letflow.Identity`, `Letflow.TenantProvisioning`) exposing: create a draft, update a draft, publish (draft -> live, sets confirmed_at), re-confirm (bumps confirmed_at on an already-live row without changing body — the explicit "I checked this, it's still accurate" action), and read (by screen_id + tenant prefix, or by process_definition_id). Every write path enforces REQ-363's sanitization rule from that design, not a weakened version of it.

NOT IN SCOPE: the tenant-facing authoring UI (REQ-365 for platform, a separate future requirement for the tenant admin UI itself — this requirement's acceptance criteria stop at a working, tested context module, callable from IEx/tests, not yet wired to any HTTP route or frontend component). Route/controller wiring, if this project's own API-surface convention wants a separate requirement for it (matching the pattern most REQ-027..030-style definition CRUD work already used), is a natural fast-follow, not bundled here — state explicitly in this requirement's close-out whether a route was added or deliberately deferred, rather than leaving it ambiguous.

result.summary: RECONSTRUCTION NOTE: this handoff was originally written live during WF02-REQ364-20260917's security-review saga as ad-hoc, non-schema JSON (informal top-level keys such as req/at/result-as-bare-string instead of HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md §2's real schema), the exact anti-pattern this session's own ISS-0692 precedent names. It has been rewritten into full schema conformance by a later ORCH session under §4.1's not_agent_attested mechanism. created_at/started_at/completed_at are all set to the file's own git-introducing-commit timestamp (`git log --follow --diff-filter=A --format=%aI --reverse -- `), the best-available real timestamp, NOT the original live dispatch/claim/completion times, which were never recorded in schema-legal fields on disk. All findings, quoted test counts, and verification detail below are migrated verbatim in substance from the original ad-hoc file; nothing was invented or paraphrased away. Commit 4ede2cc9. SCOPE TEST: APPLIES (unchanged from round 3) -- this round's diff (2388d294..4ede2cc9) touches only lib/letflow/help/help_content.ex's sanitizer logic plus tests/fixtures; no migration, no new Repo call, no new secret. INV-1/INV-4/INV-7's round-3 PASS carries forward unchanged; INV-8 is the invariant actually under test this round (blocker 3). INVARIANT ASSESSMENT: INV-1 APPLIES PASS (carried forward -- no migration/schema/prefix change in this round's diff). INV-2/INV-3/INV-5/INV-9 NOT-APPLICABLE (unchanged). INV-4 APPLIES PASS (carried forward -- no secret material touched). INV-6 meta-invariant, this handoff is the proof artifact. INV-7 APPLIES PASS (carried forward -- no Repo.query use). INV-8 APPLIES PASS -- see verification below. VERIFICATION PERFORMED: Blocker 1 reverified: Ran EarmarkParser.as_ast/2 and Letflow.Help.HelpContent.create_changeset/2 directly on '[x](javascript:alert(1))' and an all-caps variant '[x](javascript:alert(1))' -- both now valid?=false, rejected with the unsafe-scheme error. @numeric_entity_pattern confirmed changed to `~r/&#([xX][0-9a-fA-F]+|[0-9]+);/`. Genuinely closed. Blocker 2 reverified: Ran EarmarkParser.as_ast/2 on 'xy' and 'xy' -- confirmed AST still splits the raw tag across sibling text/strong/code nodes exactly as round 3 found. Ran create_changeset/2 on both: valid?=false, raw-HTML error, in both cases (including the code-span split, where flatten_plain_text/1's code-node exclusion still leaves 'y' concatenated -- still matches the tag pattern since the tag's own angle brackets are outside the excluded code content). Genuinely closed. Blocker 3 reverified: Ran create_changeset/2 on 'some text with `unclosed code' and a fenced block opened but never closed -- both now valid?=true, errors=[], no crash. Confirmed validate_markdown_safety/2 now case-matches both {:ok, ast, _} and {:error, ast, _}. Genuinely closed. All prior-round payloads retraced: reference-style link, angle-bracket autolink, backslash-before-colon, decimal entity, embedded-tab destination, plain javascript: baseline -- all still valid?=false (rejected). No regression. SEVENTH BYPASS PROBE (flatten_plain_text/1, actively probed both directions per the task brief): (a) bypass direction -- none found; flatten_plain_text/1 only ADDS a text_scan detection alongside the unchanged per-node structural checks (walk_node/1 still runs independently); it can never suppress an existing detection, and its own recursion is unconditional/whole-subtree so it cannot itself be evaded by nesting depth or additional sibling structure. (b) over-rejection direction -- CONFIRMED, but not a security-invariant violation: flatten_plain_text/1 recurses into every non-code/pre element's children and walk/1's list clause joins ALL siblings at a given level with NO separator, including the ROOT block list itself, so the projection effectively concatenates the ENTIRE document's prose (minus code/pre) into one string for the raw-tag-shape scan. Reproduced two concrete false positives new this round: (1) two adjacent paragraphs 'Configure with a<' / 'b>c or make it safe' now cross-concatenates to '...ac...' and is wrongly rejected as raw HTML; (2) ordinary prose using '<'/'>' as comparison operators split by emphasis, 'if ad then continue', is wrongly rejected the same way. (The single-leaf, no-formatting case 'if ad then continue' was ALREADY rejected before this round -- pre-existing, not new; only the cross-sibling/cross-paragraph concatenation is new.) This is a genuine availability/UX regression -- legitimate help-content authors using bare angle brackets as comparison operators or generic-type notation, split across formatting or paragraphs, will have valid drafts rejected -- but it is strictly one-directional (over-restrictive, never under-restrictive) and touches no tenant-isolation, secret, SQL-injection, or crash invariant. Not gating on it; flagged for routing. Code/pre exclusion confirmed correct at all nesting positions (structural clause-ordering check plus behavioral code-span-split payload). help_test.exs reproduced: MIX_ENV=test MIX_TEST_PARTITION=901 mix test test/letflow/help_test.exs -- real run, 'Result: 54 passed', 0 failures. Full suite reproduced: MIX_ENV=test MIX_TEST_PARTITION=901 mix test (real run, 2063s) -- 'Result: 4386/4389 passed (6/6 properties, 4380/4383 tests), 23 excluded', 3 failed. `mix test --failed` confirmed all 3 are Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckRequirementsRegistrationTest/CheckDeferralStalenessTest failures on REQ-369's docs/requirements.yaml entry missing an impl_order line -- entirely unrelated to REQ-364/help_content, matches ELIXIR-DEV's claim (already fixed on main via a merged PR this branch predates). Confirmed genuine and non-masking -- no help_content/sanitizer test among the 3. tenant_fixture.ex and table-count-assertion fixes spot-checked directly in git diff main...HEAD -- both real, matching the claims. Stale-tenant_template-schema claim not independently reproducible after the fact (a prior-state DB artifact, not a code diff) but consistent with observed clean behavior this round.

issues.description: flatten_plain_text/1's whole-subtree, no-separator concatenation creates false-positive raw-HTML rejections for legitimate content containing bare '<'/'>' characters split across inline formatting or paragraph boundaries -- an availability/UX defect, not a security bypass (only over-rejects, never under-rejects).
